# Safehire.ai Raises £500k Seed  
Safehire.ai raises £500k in follow-on seed funding to scale its digital risk screening platform for high-trust enterprise hiring and workforce assurance.  
Safehire.ai Raises £500k Seed  
Safehire.ai, a London-based digital risk screening company, has secured £500k in follow-on funding to scale its platform. This latest investment, which follows an earlier £1.05m round in April 2025, brings the company total funding to £1.55 million.
## Safehire.ai Use of Funds  
The new capital will be used to scale the company's Digital Risk Screening platform beyond the education sector, support larger enterprise use cases, develop insider risk capabilities, and prepare for international expansion.  
About Safehire.ai  
Founded in 2025 by Simon Holden and Sean Lumley, Safehire.ai provides an AI-powered Digital Risk Screening platform. By combining large language models with human analysis, the company helps organizations identify digital risks across surface, deep, and dark web sources to support high-trust hiring and workforce assurance decisions.

This round, together with the €1.22 million (£1.05 million) Seed investment round closed in April 2025, brings total investment to €1.8 million (£1.55 million).
Safehire.ai was founded in 2024 by former British Army officers Simon Holden and Sean Lumley. Holden is a former school bursar and cybersecurity founder who saw the digital risk visibility gap facing education first-hand, and Lumley is a serial technology entrepreneur and co-founder of CybSafe, a human risk management and behavioural cybersecurity platform. The company states that it provides digital risk screening for high-trust hiring, safeguarding and workforce assurance decisions.
At a time when the digital risk surface around people has become far more complex, fragmented and difficult to assess, searches are often conducted by untrained HR personnel, while those conducted in a traditional manner by professional vetting staff might cost £1,500 per search,” Safehire.ai mentioned in a press release. The UK startup highlighted that its Digital Risk Screening (DRS) platform first searches open-source data on the surface, deep and dark web, then applies AI-enriched context to the raw data before finally integrating human analyst verification to produce evidence‑based digital intelligence packaged into easy-to-understand background risk reports.
DRS enables organisations to conduct over 10,000 searches per day, instead of the 15 searches a single human analyst can achieve, and at a fraction of the cost. The company reported that one large multi-academy trust said using Safehire.ai DRS checks saved its HR team an average of 1 hour per candidate.
